info.description: REST access to the same datasets as the Tapetide MCP server, with the same token and the same quota. Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; personal tokens are created at https://tapetide.com/settings/tokens. Every successful data request costs one unit from your plan's daily and monthly quota (free tier: 50/day, no monthly cap). Failed requests are refunded. Responses are complete documents: nothing is truncated to fit, and routes that page say so in `meta`. Data is for information only and is not investment advice.

get.description: Search ~8,000 Indian stocks by name, symbol, BSE code or ISIN. Common brand names and post-rename aliases match too (Zomato finds ETERNAL, Infosys finds INFY), and queries of 4 or more characters tolerate typos. Listed companies rank first, then by match quality (exact symbol or code, prefix, word, contains), with larger companies first within each tier. Delisted companies are included after listed ones. Use the returned `symbol` with the per-stock routes.

get.description: Row-per-day OHLCV: date, open, high, low, close (split/bonus-adjusted), `raw_close` (unadjusted, null where no raw print exists) and volume. `days` sets the lookback window (default 365, max 2000); `interval` is the bar size (daily or weekly). `meta.window` states the window actually served and `next_cursor` gives the `end_date` for the preceding page, so a multi-year series is paged with `end_date` until `has_more` is false. Without `end_date`, a stock whose last bar is older than the window (delisted or long suspended) is served the window ending at its last bar, flagged `meta.window.anchored_to_last_bar: true`.

parameters.name: interval
parameters.description: Bar size: daily (default) or weekly. Intraday bars are not served here.

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: Inclusive YYYY-MM-DD upper bound; the paging cursor. Pass `meta.window.next_cursor` from the previous page.

raw_close.null_semantics: NULL means NO RAW PRINT IS AVAILABLE for that bar. It is never a zero, never a placeholder, and must not be substituted with `close` — `close` is back-adjusted, so doing so would silently mix two price scales.
raw_close.reconstruction_alternative: where raw_close is null, a raw series can still be reconstructed from the split/bonus adjustment factors via raw(d) = adjusted(d) / cumulative_factor(d).

window.counts_note: returned_rows/total_matching_rows count stored bars matching this query. Neither is an assertion of how many bars SHOULD exist — that would need per-security listing/suspension data we do not have for the whole universe.

Where more than one reading exists for the same metric and period, a populated value is preferred over an empty one, then a figure read from the company's own machine-readable results filing over the compiled datasets (from that filing's date on; an `as_of` before it returns the compiled figure), then a non-zero value over a 0 (one dataset rounds to whole crore, so small figures can read 0 there), then the primary dataset over the secondary, then the most recently published reading on or before `as_of`. A reported 0 that means "not reported" is not published as a value: periods where total assets, total liabilities or share capital read 0 are omitted, revenue reading 0 while the same period shows non-zero operating expenses is published as `value: null`, and a period whose every income-statement amount reads 0 (a period the company did not report, e.g. before listing) publishes `value: null` for all its income-statement metrics.
